summary: Researched the evening before (Sat 21 Nov); lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the morning check and the final check. Sunday has Serie A, La Liga, Ligue 1 and Premier League football, seven NFL games and one NHL game; basketball is not researched (the owner's permanent rule). Medium: Juventus, Barcelona, Brighton (at Hull), Inter (at Atalanta), Marseille, and in the NFL the Bears, Cowboys, Lions, Jaguars and Steelers, plus the Lightning in the NHL. Low: Paris FC (ClubElo and the Sports Mole model about 15 points under the market), Milan (price down 3.1% in 24h with no news) and the Chargers (a 1-8 favourite at about 60%). Excluded as derbies or fierce rivalries on a conservative reading: Getafe v Atlético (Madrid-area derby) and Broncos v Raiders (historic AFC West rivalry). Views that contradicted a game's own main risk were dropped (Barcelona over 2.5, Juventus over 1.5, Inter over 2.5 and both teams to score).

checks.team_news: ESPN game summary injuries (read 21 Nov): Bears list CB Kyler Gordon Out (shoulder), WR Zavion Thomas Questionable (ankle), RB Zavier Scott, DT Kentavius Street and OT Braxton Jones on IR. Saints list OT Asim Richards, C Erik McCoy, OT Taliese Fuaga and CB Martin Emerson Jr. all Out, LB Pete Werner Questionable (hamstring). No quarterback appears on either injury list. The Saints' Thursday report (neworleanssaints.com) also shows DT Jeffery Simmons (knee) limited for the Bears and WR Luther Burden (concussion) and RB Kyle Monangai (toe) full for the Bears. I did not find the Bears' Friday final statuses beyond ESPN's list, so Simmons's status is unconfirmed. The Saints are missing three starting offensive linemen.
checks.lineups: Not confirmed (inactives come about 90 minutes before kick-off). ESPN's scoreboard leaders show Caleb Williams (1546 yds, 8 TD, 5 INT) for the Bears and Tyler Shough (2173 yds, 15 TD, 7 INT) for the Saints as the starting QBs, and neither is on an injury list. The Saints' offensive line will be heavily patched (Fuaga, McCoy, Richards out). Only one source (ESPN) for the QBs.
checks.rotation: The Bears had a bye in Week 10 (no game on 15 Nov); their last game was a 27-24 win over TB on 9 Nov, and they are at home with extra rest. The Saints played at Carolina on 15 Nov (17-20 loss), travel to Chicago on a normal week and play Cincinnati next, then Green Bay. The Bears play Detroit on Thanksgiving (26 Nov), a short week next, so a slight look-ahead is possible but no rest of starters is expected.
checks.motivation: Bears 7-2 (4-1 home), in the NFC playoff race; Saints 3-6 (1-5 home, 2-1 road) and out of the race. The favourite has plenty to play for. Nothing points to a fully motivated underdog.
checks.form: Bears last 5: W 31-17 at ATL... exact results from the ESPN schedule: W 31-23 ATL (18 Oct), W 30-24 NE, W 34-17 at SEA, W 27-24 TB, so 4 straight wins before the bye; earlier L 7-31 at GB (11 Oct), and a 3-9 loss to MIN (20 Sep). Saints last 5: L 20-17 at CAR (15 Nov), W 23-22 CLE (8 Nov), L 10-16 PIT, W 34-27 NYG, L 13-23 MIN; they have 3 wins in 9 games and allowed 45 to ATL. Bears 7-2 vs Saints 3-6.
checks.h2h: Last meeting 19 Oct 2025 at Soldier Field: Bears won 26-14 (Rotowire). No 2026 meeting before this one. Style: Bears' run game (Swift 576 yds, 10 TD) against a Saints line missing three starters.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (read 21 Nov): Bears moneyline -630, Saints +461; de-vigged Bears 0.829, Saints 0.171 (sum of raw implied 1.041). Spread Bears -11.5 (-107), total 48.5. Opening line was Bears -278 ML and -6.5, so the market has moved strongly towards the Bears (consistent with the three Saints offensive linemen out). Polymarket 0.845 agrees within 2 points of DraftKings. Polymarket 24h move: 0.845 to 0.845 (0% change, from data.move_24h). No price drift against the favourite.
checks.models: ESPN Matchup Predictor (summary endpoint): Bears 78.6%, Saints 21.2%. No ClubElo or DVOA read. Point differential from the ESPN schedule: Bears strongly positive, Saints negative.
checks.venue_weather: Soldier Field, Chicago, outdoor grass, not neutral (ESPN neutralSite false). ESPN weather block: 56 F, gusts 21 mph, precipitation chance 56. Windy and possibly wet conditions help the underdog slightly by shortening the game. Note that ESPN lists the Bears as the home side and Polymarket names the Saints first, so the candidate keys are home=Saints, away=Bears.

games.reason: The Bears are 7-2 at home against a 3-6 Saints side missing three offensive linemen. The DraftKings de-vigged price (0.829) and ESPN's predictor (78.6%) both support the Polymarket 0.845, so the price is slightly rich but within range. The confidence is medium because the starting QBs and Friday final statuses are not confirmed, the spread of -11.5 leaves room for a late game, and the Bears have a Thanksgiving game on Thursday.
games.main_risk: Close game decided late: Caleb Williams turnovers (5 INT) and wind of 21 mph with possible rain on a 11.5-point spread keep the score tight, and a mid-week look-ahead to Detroit on Thanksgiving. Backup-QB risk is low on the evidence (neither QB on the injury list) but inactives are not out yet.

games.reason: HARD rule "derby or fierce rivalry", conservative reading (as for Getafe v Atlético the same day): Broncos-Raiders is a historic AFC West rivalry with its own Wikipedia article (73-58-2 series, a 2017 sideline brawl, the 1995 Shanahan dispute, the most Monday Night Football meetings in NFL history). The research otherwise found Denver a clear favourite (7-2, 4-0 at home, rested after a bye; DraftKings about 0.824 de-vigged, ESPN FPI about 86%) against a 4-6 Raiders side with a rookie QB.
games.main_risk: A close, low-scoring division game (total 40.5) decided late or by turnovers: Nix has 4 interceptions, a rookie Mendoza can still hit a big play against Denver, and rivalry games are tighter than the ratings suggest. A late scratch to Nix is the other risk (not on the injury report, inactives not yet out). Rivalry classification is a judgement call: it counts as a notable divisional rivalry, not a derby.

Villarreal are 9th on 15 points from 12 games and have nothing secured. They are not in a relegation fight either. Not a derby; the Derbi de la Comunitat is Villarreal vs Valencia. Neither head coach was changed in the last 30 days; Inigo Perez took over from Marcelino in the summer.
checks.form: Barcelona: won 10 of their first 11 La Liga games, the only league loss being the Clasico. Recent results include a 2-1 win at Atletico and a 6-1 win over Alaves. Khelnow's form string is W-W-W-L-L, including losses to Real Madrid and PSG. Villarreal: no win in their first 5 league games, then 4 wins in 7, including 2-0 over Getafe and 2-1 over Valencia. A 6-0 loss to PSG appears in the Khelnow form list. I found no xG data.
checks.h2h: 58 meetings: Barcelona 36 wins, Villarreal 12, 10 draws (about 17% draws). Barcelona won both league meetings last season. Previews (Khelnow, Sportskeeda) predict 3-1.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/esp.1/scoreboard?dates=20261122): Barcelona 1.20 (-500), draw 7.5 (+650 on the live feed), Villarreal 12.0. De-vigged home 79.4%, draw 12.7%, away 7.9%; total line 4.5 goals. Polymarket home is 81.4%, about 2 points above DraftKings, so the second price agrees within 5 points. The Polymarket 24h move is flat (0.815 to 0.815, 0% change). DraftKings opening home was also 1.20; Villarreal drifted from 9.5 to 12, which favours Barcelona. No price move against the favourite.
checks.models: ClubElo API returned nothing, so there is no bookmaker-free rating. The only independent evidence is the league table (Barcelona GD +35 vs Villarreal +2 in 12 games) and the previews' 3-1 predictions. This check is only partly filled.
checks.venue_weather: Spotify Camp Nou, Barcelona, kick-off 13:00 UTC (14:00 local). A normal home venue. I found no weather or pitch concerns, but also no forecast.

games.reason: A strong home favourite, top of the table, with a real title incentive against a mid-table side that has nothing at stake. DraftKings (79.4% de-vigged) agrees with Polymarket (81.4%) within 2 points, and the 24h price move is zero. No hard exclusion applies: it is not a derby, no coach change, and a normal venue. Confidence is medium rather than high because lineups are unconfirmed, the centre-back news is conflicting (Cubarsi), and no Elo rating could be read.
games.main_risk: A draw or an away win, most likely through a low-scoring game where Barcelona create chances but Villarreal sit deep, or through defensive weakness if Cubarsi is out. Barcelona already have a league loss and two recent defeats (Real Madrid, PSG) in the form string. A one-goal win would sink the -1.5 handicap and the Over 2.5 goals leg, so I give no view on the handicaps or Barcelona team-goals legs.

checks.h2h: No recent meetings found; style matchup is Dallas' high-scoring offense against a Titans defense allowing 390.9 yards per game (Fox Sports), while Dallas' own defense is the worst in the league on yards. SI projects an over (total 54.5).
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN: Cowboys ML 1.28 (-356) vs Titans 3.83, de-vigged Cowboys 0.749 (opening 1.34/3.35, so the line moved toward Dallas); spread DAL -7.5 (open -6.5), total 54.5 (open 48.5). SI shows -425/+330 and -8.5 from another snapshot. Polymarket 0.775 is 2.6 points above the DK de-vig, within 5 points. Polymarket 24h move: 0.775 to 0.775 (0%), no drift against the favourite.

games.reason: Dallas hosts a 1-8 Titans side with the 29th-31st ranked roster, needs the win for the NFC East chase, has no QB doubt and the books and Opta agree at about 75-78%. The Titans' offence has scored 23+ in four straight games.
games.main_risk: Dallas' defence is the league's worst by yards and points allowed (28.2 per game), and the Cowboys are 1-4 at home with no back-to-back wins; with TE Ferguson and WR Mingo out, a shootout that Tennessee wins or stays close in late is the main failure path, along with turnovers (Prescott 6 INT, Ward 6 INT). Cowboys' price is ahead of DraftKings by 2.6 points, so p is trimmed.

I found no midweek or cup fixture for either side, and I did not find their next fixtures. No rotation is reported. checks.motivation: ESPN standings before the game: Paris FC 3rd, 20 pts from 10 games (6W 2D 2L), GD +7, unbeaten at home in the league per Sports Mole. Angers 17th, 8 pts, GD -10, six points above bottom side Le Havre, winless in five and without a goal in their last three league games. Gilli coached Paris FC until Feb 2026, a mild storyline but not a derby.

checks.h2h: Angers won 1-0 in Aug 2025 and the sides drew 0-0 in Jan 2026, with Gilli then at Paris FC. Paris FC failed to score in both meetings. Both were tight, low-scoring games and one ended level, which is a draw and low-scoring warning for this game.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds): home 1.32, draw 5.5, away 9.0, de-vigged 72.1/17.3/10.6, opening 1.34/5.0/8.0, so the favourite's price shortened slightly. There is no move against the favourite and no unexplained drift.

Sports Mole's model: 57.9/24.1/18.0, with a most likely score of 1-0, BTTS 50.3% and over 2.5 at 51.6%. Both are about 15 points below the market win price and put the draw at 24-26%, so p is cut to the 5-point floor.
checks.venue_weather: Stade Jean-Bouin, Paris, normal home venue (ESPN). Kick-off 15:00 local, referee Aurelien Petit (eurofootnews). I found no weather forecast or pitch report, so I cannot confirm conditions, but nothing unusual was reported.

games.reason: No hard exclusion applies: the fixture, venue and date are verified, there is no coach change in the last 7 days, no confirmed rotation, and the table shows Paris FC 3rd chasing a podium against 17th-placed Angers who need points. DraftKings (72%) agrees with Polymarket (74.5%) within 2 points and the price is stable. Confidence is medium only because the bookmaker-free models (ClubElo 59%, Sports Mole 58%) sit about 15 points under the market and put the draw at 24-26%, so p is set at the 5-point floor. A Paris FC win is still the most likely result. Set to low when merged: the two bookmaker-free models sit about 15 points under the market, a doubt the 5-point limit on p cannot reflect, and Paris FC failed to score in both recent meetings.
games.main_risk: A draw or a narrow home win: past meetings were 1-0 and 0-0, Paris FC were held scoreless in both, and both bookmaker-free models put the draw at 24-26% against about 17% in the market. Paris FC also have fitness doubts (Camara, Chergui; Ikone and Sangui out) and the lineup is unconfirmed. Angers have scored three goals in five games, which makes goal legs risky when the game ends 1-0.

Some Juventus players returned late from national teams (Lucumi from Colombia, McKennie from the USA), and Gatti is rested. No midweek European fixture was found for either side. Venezia: 6 points from 11 games, 8 goals scored in 11, no away points yet (livetipsportal). Under Nicola they took 3 points from 4 games (beat Napoli, lost to Genoa, Inter and Como). Pazzidifanta says Nicola's side beat Udinese and ended a run of three defeats. I found no xG data.

checks.venue_weather: Allianz Stadium, Turin, Juventus home ground, a normal venue. Kick-off 12:30 local on Sunday 22 Nov (11:30 UTC). I did not read a weather forecast; no pitch problem or extreme weather was reported.

games.reason: The fixture is verified (Serie A matchday 12, 12:30 at the Allianz Stadium). No hard rule applies. Nicola was appointed on 14 Oct 2026, 38 days ago, so there is no coach-change exclusion. Juventus are the home favourite with Polymarket and DraftKings agreeing within about 3 points, and the price has been stable. Venezia are 19th, without an away point and with a poor goal difference. Confidence is medium and not high because Juventus have flank absences, the lineup and shape are uncertain, they are only 8th with a +3 goal difference, the recent 2-2 draw with Fiorentina shows they do not always win, and no Elo or other independent rating could be read. p is set slightly below the market, in line with the DraftKings de-vig.

Juventus have injuries and doubts on the flanks (Kalulu out, Cambiaso and Celik training apart, Nico Gonzalez a doubt), a changed shape, and players back late from national teams. A 1-0 or 1-1 result fails both the favourite's margin legs and the over legs. Handicap legs such as -1.5 are at risk for the same reason.
